newsitem.title: USA: Clinton proposes increased budget for crime, drugs.
newsitem.headline: Clinton proposes increased budget for crime, drugs.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday proposed a $19.3 billion budget for the U.S. Justice Department for 1998, with big increases to fight crime, drugs, youth violence, terrorism and illegal immigration.
In unveiling the budget proposals, which must be approved by the Republican-controlled Congress, Attorney General Janet Reno said the increased spending will focus on her top priorities.
"Our 1998 budget request will enable us to continue our battles against youth violence, illicit drugs, terrorism and illegal immigration," she told a news conference.
Justice Department officials said its total budget has soared nearly 70 percent since Clinton took office in 1993, the biggest increase for any Cabinet agency.

Among the proposals, the Justice Department seeks a $233 million increase to crack down on gangs and youth violence, a 13 percent rise in the Immigration and Naturalisation Service budget and more money to hire new Drug Enforcement Administration and FBI agents.
As part of the nearly $390 million for counter-terrorism programmes, department officials proposed adding 23 more FBI agents and opening eight new offices around the world.
Those offices, to be staffed with FBI agents, would be located in Brazil, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Kazakhstan, South Korea, Nigeria, Turkey and Uzbekistan, according to budget documents.

The Clinton administration, which came under criticism from some Republicans in Congress last year for not doing enough to fight drugs, proposed more money for investigating and prosecuting drug cases.
Reno said the 4.2 percent rise in funding to fight drugs would provide for 168 Drug Enforcement Administration agents, 56 FBI agents and 37 more federal prosecutors.

The boost in the immigration agency's budget, totalling a record $3.6 billion, called for 500 additional U.S. Border Patrol agents and 277 immigration inspectors, she said. The Justice Department also plans to spend $500 million to reimburse states for the cost of jailing illegal immigrants.
Among other highlights in the budget proposals were the following:
-- The FBI would get $32 million, for a three-year total of $130 million, to complete the construction of its new crime laboratory.
-- The number of Justice Department employees would go up to 121,000, from 110,000 now.
-- An additional 17,000 police officers would be put on the streets. That would bring funding for a total of 80,000 officers out of the 100,000 that Clinton has promised under a 1994 law.
